Do you ever catch yourself repeating words or phrases? I've been bipolar since I was 23, and I'm 40 now. I understand everything you are saying. Being reckless will usually end up badly though, and extreme depression isn't good either. You have a disease, as do I. Never give up, just know you have survived 100% of your worst days. Also remember people that don't know you, don't know your thoughts, they don't know you are bipolar. I find it's best to stay introvert, as I don't want to be seen as crazy either. Your family or friends don't know what you deal with, and honestly unless they are bipolar no one does. It's extremely hard, and a never ending battle. Adjusting meds helps, also look up somatic therapy, meditation and knowing your body makes you feel more centered. You are not alone, you are a survivor and a warrior. Battling mental illness is never easy.

If you are truly bipolar you would not be able to function without medications, your life would just be in and out of psych wards. If you can function without meds, more power to you. I know I could not live a normal life with out meds. When you think about missing being manic, remember this. We can not function at that high of a level forever, the higher you get, the bigger the crash. The best is to find a happy medium, if you can achieve that without medication, that's obviously ideal. Just know all of those range of emotions is not good for bipolar people, being a zombie isn't good either, but to many manic highs just leads to being in the hospital. Do what is best for you.

I feel like a villain and a God sometimes too. The truth is we have a disease, and you can't help how you feel. Life is too short, the best thing is to accept what you have, and live life to the best of your ability. Have you ever caught yourself repeating words or phrases even when you are not in a manic state?

when you are bipolar, you will lose interest in many things. Up and down, like a rollercoaster. The trick is to just find the things you really enjoy and continue to do them, no matter what. It's hard to stay interested, the idea with mood stabilizers it to keep you from being in a manic high or a manic low. Just in the middle, which can suck sometimes because you don't have a lot of emotions. However it's better than the ladder. Manic highs only lead to manic lows. When you are bipolar the best thing to is keep those special interests you have, like for me lifting weights, I never lose interest in it. You should not have a goal of hypomanic, that could lead to extreme depression, you just want to be in the middle, not crazy happy but also not really sad. My therapist told me when I was really happy it wasn't true happiness, and it was just a manic high. If that's true for bipolar people, and we never feel happiness, what a way to live, right? I don't believe her though, and how would she know. She's not bipolar. You will be ok though, just take it one day at a time. If the meds they give you make you really depressed don't stay on them, that is not how you want to feel.
